text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT PAGE · GPU_POOL_EXHAUSTION · Sev2 · paging @oncall
incident-bot: Symptoms: sustained queue growth on gpu-pool-west, requester throttling (429s) and increased p95 response times. Autoscaler reports at max nodes=40. Link: https://internal.redwood/incident/1774123456

sara (oncall): ack. I'm on it. seeing lots of pending pods in the model-runner replicaset and a spike in `model-request-queue`. Customers hitting 429s. Will gather quick triage.

mike (infra): digging into cluster autoscaler + nodepool. `kubectl get nodes -l pool=gpu-west --no-headers | wc -l` -> 40 (matches maxNodes). HPA on model-runner shows target 70% CPU but pod limit `maxReplicas=200` is fine. Problem is nodepool maxNodes=40.

alan (runtime): confirm queue growth on the GPU side (KV cache pressure + long sequence requests). We have a burst workload from a few high-latency customers causing KV cache thrash. Immediate need: temporary capacity increase so we don't drop requests.

tess (eng-sre): oncall handoff to @kumar for manual override. I'll prepare comms and monitor throttles. @sara can you post short customer-facing blurb after we confirm impact?

sara (oncall): yup. short blurb ready to paste once we have ETA.

kumar (sre): I can do the manual cap raise. Who's authorized for emergency manual changes? Need approval from ops director to modify nodepool limits.

nina (director-ops): Nina here — approve emergency manual increase to 60 nodes for 30m window for production gpu-pool-west. Please document the change and rollback plan.

kumar (sre): executing now. command:
```
gcloud container node-pools update gpu-pool-west \ 
  --cluster=prod-cluster-west \ 
  --max-nodes=60 --region=us-west1
```
Running... should take a few mins for node autoscaler to accept new limit.

mike (infra): pre-flight checks: quota looks OK, driver daemonset tolerations set, GPU quotas available. starting to see new nodes provisioning.

incident-bot: New nodes detected: 8 nodes are provisioning. Current nodes: 48/60.

alan (runtime): restarting a subset of pods to rebalance KV caches across new nodes. Command: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/model-runner -n prod --timeout=5m` to avoid mass eviction.

sara (oncall): posting to status page draft:
"We are experiencing degraded performance and request throttling for certain GPU-backed model endpoints due to capacity pressure. We are applying an emergency capacity increase; some requests may still be delayed while the pool scales. Updates to follow." :hourglass_flowing_sand:

olivia (customer-success): bumped — several enterprise customers reported 429s and a few timeouts. I'm sending a heads-up to top 5 affected accounts with short note.

kumar (sre): scale operation completed: node count = 60. `kubectl get nodes -l pool=gpu-west --no-headers | wc -l` -> 60. New pods scheduling. Queue length starting to drop.

mike (infra): verifying autoscaler settings. Current autoscaler config had `maxNodes: 40`. We bumped to 60 manually; need follow-up to ensure CA doesn't reset this inadvertently and to ensure proper IAM notes.

alan (runtime): p95 latencies trending down from 7s -> 1.2s over last 6m. 429s rate reduced by ~92%. Good mitigation.

tess (eng-sre): handoff summary for next shift: manual cap raise executed after approval, nodes scaled to 60, restarted model-runner gradually, KV cache warmed across nodes. Primary contributing factors: sudden burst of long-sequence inference for a small customer cohort + conservative autoscaler maxNodes.

sara (oncall): posting status update: "Incident mitigated — capacity increased and throttles reduced. We are monitoring for recurrence."

nina (director-ops): please open follow-up ticket to adjust autoscaler policy + add runbook for emergency manual cap raises. Also add alert for queue growth hitting 70% of node capacity earlier.

kumar (sre): created follow-up: INC-2026 - increase gpu-pool maxNodes to 80 after capacity planning meeting; add automated emergency override playbook; add postmortem.

olivia (customer-success): thanks team — I'll update customers who opened tickets. Send me the postmortem link when available.

tess (eng-sre): postmortem owners: alan (root cause analysis) + mike (infra changes) + sara (customer comms). ETA for PM: 48 hours.

sara (oncall): handing off to night oncall @mike for monitoring. I'm logging out. Good job everyone. :thumbsup:

mike (infra): ack handoff. I'll keep a 2h watch and rollback cap to 40 after we confirm stable traffic? Need ops sign-off for rollback.

nina (director-ops): approve rollback window: if metrics stable for 1h, authorized rollback to previous baseline (40) with 30m cooldown. Otherwise keep raised and discuss at 09:00 ops sync.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED · Severity downgraded to S3 for monitoring. Final note: manual cap raise documented in INC-2026."
